items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: The interviewee discusses Fazzola's influence on other musicians (Fountain, Jug Burger) but does not describe a personal interaction or professional relationship with Fazzola himself.

ctx.x: No. I detect no... Influence of Fountain's playing on anybody around. I... It's interesting to wonder about who influenced him. Uh-huh. But it seems to me that he's a... An accomplished...

Well, let's... Let's go back a few years. Uh... It's possible that, uh... Uh... Fountain was influenced by, uh... A player that he admired very much, and we did get to know, uh... Fazzola. Uh... Do you think there's such a thing as a Fazzola influence in Chicago today?

Yeah. The name Jug Burger springs to mind. Uh-huh. Uh... Jug was very fond of... What was his nickname? Foz? Yes. And, uh... And Jug, I believe, is from New Orleans, or from Biloxi, or that neck of the woods. And he was very... Very fond of Foz. And his playing does reflect Foz's playing. But... I don't know if anybody can really do what Fozola did. I don't think Fountain does it. Although I think the influence is detectable there.
